haiku-low.q1: No. Cursors go only through Redis. They are never sent to the document service or stored in Postgres.
haiku-low.q2: At most one per 60 ms, plus one trailing message. The server silently drops any message under 50 ms after the last accepted one from that connection.
haiku-low.q3: It holds the cursor, replacing any older held cursor, and draws it once it has applied that revision.
haiku-low.q4: If within 500 revisions, it transforms the position to appliedRev and draws it. If older than that (HistoryGone), the caret is removed until the sender's next update.
haiku-low.q5: Each tab has its own connId, so it shows as separate entries under one userId. The user is listed while any connId remains, and disappears when the last one is removed or expires.
haiku-low.q6: After a clean tab close, well under 2 seconds. After the gateway node dies, at most about 35 seconds plus delivery, within the 45-second limit.
haiku-low.q7: In Redis: a sorted set presence:{docId} and a hash cursors:{docId}, per userId|connId. Each pong refreshes the entry to 30 s expiry and the keys to 60 s.
haiku-low.q8: Nothing runs on the dead node. Its entries expire within 30 s, then a surviving node's sweep (every 5 s per document) removes them and publishes leave events to clients.
haiku-low.q9: The accepted cursor is saved and published on pres:{docId}. Every node with local sockets on the document, including the sender's node, forwards it to its clients.
haiku-low.q10: The client subscribes to pres:{docId} before the register script reads the snapshot. Events during the read are harmless, since connIds are never reused and repeated join or leave changes nothing.
haiku-low.q11: The register script returns every live entry with its cursor, sent as a snapshot, so idle users' carets appear immediately.
haiku-low.q12: It ignores any cursor whose seq is not higher than the highest seq already taken for that connId. Held cursors count as taken.

sonnet.q1: No. Cursors never go to the document service and never touch Postgres. They go through Redis only (cursors:{docId} hash plus pub/sub).
sonnet.q2: Client sends at most one cursor message per 60 ms, plus one trailing message so the last position isn't lost. The node drops silently anything arriving under 50 ms after the last accepted message on that connection.
sonnet.q3: It holds the cursor, replacing any older held cursor, and draws it once it has applied that rev.
sonnet.q4: If rev <= appliedRev, it draws at transformPosition(pos, rev, appliedRev). If the rev is more than 500 revisions behind, transformPosition throws HistoryGone and the caret is removed until the sender's next update.
sonnet.q5: Shown once. Each tab has its own connId; the presence store maps userId to a set of connIds. The user disappears only when that set is empty, i.e. after leave events for all their connIds.
sonnet.q6: Clean tab close: well under 2 s. Node death: within the 45 s limit (worst case about 35 s plus delivery: up to 30 s expiry plus up to 5 s until the next sweep).
sonnet.q7: In Redis: presence:{docId} sorted set with one member userId|connId per connection (score = expiry time), plus cursors:{docId} hash. Entries are kept fresh by the node's heartbeat: each pong (ping every 10 s) triggers a refresh script setting expiry to now+30 s and pushing both keys' expiry to 60 s.
sonnet.q8: The entries expire (no refresh, within 30 s). A surviving node's sweep script (every 5 s per doc with local sockets) removes expired entries and their cursors, and that node publishes a leave for each removed entry, which nodes forward to their clients.
sonnet.q9: The accepted cursor is saved in cursors:{docId} and published on Redis channel pres:{docId}. Every node with a local socket on that doc is subscribed and forwards it to its clients. The document does not say anything different for the sender's own node; it is also subscribed, so it gets it via the same channel (not explicitly stated). The sender ignores its own userId's cursor.
sonnet.q10: The node subscribes to pres:{docId} first, then runs the register script to read the snapshot. Events arriving during the read are harmless since connIds are never reused, so repeated join/leave change nothing.
sonnet.q11: The register script returns every live entry with its cursor from the cursors hash, and the node sends it as a snapshot, so the full list and everyone's caret, including idle users, arrive at once.
sonnet.q12: Each cursor carries a per-connection seq (+1 per message). The receiver ignores a cursor whose seq is not higher than the highest seq already taken for that connId (a held cursor counts as taken). It keeps these seq records even across a snapshot replace.
